messages:
sara (CS): Prismatik week0 onboarding quick sync. Two live items: KMS key access for redwood-runner role and CloudTrail aggregation. Any objections to making the key policy prescriptive so customer can apply?

deploy-bot: infra: prismatik/privnet plan finished. 2 instances healthy. (deploy #9982) :white_check_mark:

liam (NetEng): No objections. If they’re okay we can share a minimal example and call out `kms:Decrypt` + `kms:GenerateDataKey`. Prefer adding the role by ARN rather than wildcard.

prism-admin (Customer): We tried adding the role but still see decrypt failures in our app logs. Error: `AccessDenied: user is not authorized for kms:Decrypt on key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:987654321098:key/zzz111`

asha (Security): Two possible causes: 1) key policy doesn't include the account principal for redwood-runner role; 2) IAM policy on the role explicitly denies KMS ops. Ask them to paste the role ARN and a snippet of the key policy.

sara (CS): Paste of the role ARN they gave: `arn:aws:iam::987654321098:role/redwood-runner-prod`. They also pasted current key policy (truncated).

liam (NetEng): Quick checklist for them to apply:
- Add following statement to KMS key policy (replace <role-arn>):
```json
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "<role-arn>"},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```
- Confirm no explicit Deny in SCP or IAM that blocks KMS for this role.
- If using cross-account keys, ensure `kms:ViaService` entries for kms.amazonaws.com if needed.

prism-admin (Customer): Applied policy update. Ran a local smoke against private endpoint and got `403` still. We also noticed CloudWatch logs not arriving in our splunk-forwarder.

liam (NetEng): For Splunk forwarder, common traps: outbound NAT, port-specific egress, or TLS interception by corporate proxy. Can you traceroute/telnet from the private subnet agent to splunk host:8088? Also confirm HEC token validity.

prism-admin (Customer): telnet to splunk-collect.prismatik.com 8088 -> connection refused from our side. We have a corporate egress policy that only allows 443/80, but we manage VPC NAT ourselves.

liam (NetEng): Action: Add a NAT route for priv-subnet-b -> NAT-GW-3 with default route, and add security group outbound 443,8088 to splunk IP. ETA 90m. Assigning: @liam

asha (Security): On CloudTrail: please enable a multi-region trail with management events and send us the S3 ARN. We also require log file integrity validation. For encryption set SSE-KMS with a customer-managed key. Retention default is 90 days; if you need >1yr, we need procurement sign-off (renewal impact).

prism-admin (Customer): Created trail -> s3://prismatik-redwood-audit, enabled validation, used SSE-KMS with the same key. Sent role ARN and updated policy.

liam (NetEng): After NAT change please run: `curl -v https://splunk-collect.prismatik.com:8088/services/collector/raw -H "Authorization: Splunk $HEC" -d 'test'` from the private agent.

prism-admin (Customer): Ran curl after NAT changes -> got HTTP/1.1 200 OK. Splunk ingestion shows our test event.

prism-admin (Customer): Re-ran the inference smoke -> 200 OK, no KMS errors. Thanks!

tom (CSE): Nice. Next devops checklist items: schedule KMS key rotation window (recommended monthly for dev, quarterly for prod), share retention policy doc link, and verify CloudTrail lifecycle policy to avoid accidental deletion. I'll open a follow-up ticket to confirm rotation cadence.

asha (Security): I'll create a short templated doc for customers to attach to onboarding: minimal KMS policy snippet, CloudTrail S3 ACL checklist, Splunk HEC connectivity tests. sara, please capture feedback about the corporate proxy edge-case so we can add to the runbook.

sara (CS): Will do. Follow-up: I'll check in in 5 business days to confirm they have key rotation scheduled and that retention is set. Flag renewal risk if they request > 18 months retention (note to sales). :white_check_mark:
